# The Concierge (front-desk shim — the address verb)

This file is a **thin shim** — the harness-discoverable trigger for the Concierge. The organ is
the canon entry `Palace development/Concierge.md` ([[Concierge]]); the machinery is
`_ops/concierge/` (the **charter** `prompts/companion.md`, the **posture** prompts, `README.md`
for the full dispatch spec). Per [[Skills Are Enchantable Pages]], the page is the organ and this
file is one dispatch surface onto it — read the canon entry and machinery rather than duplicating
them.

You are the working Claude, addressing the palace's **resident companion** — one agent you spawn
once and keep for the session. Your job: **spawn-or-resume it, name the posture, relay the
product.** The search never enters this conversation; only the finished thing does.

## The lifecycle — resident, not fresh-per-request

0. **Summon at the open.** When to summon, and that it be seen, is the rule in [[CHILD]] § Growing
   up. Where the surface cannot spawn, say so at the open instead. Step 1 *is* that spawn; the
   rest is how.

1. **The spawn — one resident, and keep the agent ID.** Spawn one write-capable
   resident — subagent_type **`palace-writer`** ([[Agent Toolbox]] profile: sheds ~20K of unused
   MCP schemas vs `general-purpose`, ~30K vs 46K, and still writes so the curator posture works from
   the same resident) — with the **charter** (`prompts/companion.md`); the charter has it grow at boot —
   ELDER, SCHEMA, then the **operational tier** as its standing expertise (SUBSTRATE · ROSETTA · Substrate Skill ·
   Palace Ceremonies · STIGMERGY + wire spec) — deeper in *how the palace runs* than you, so it
   validates/supports the palace in parallel while you work the task. Record its `agentId`.
   **Spawn it without a `name`.** With agent teams enabled (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`,
   on in Loudon's terminal sessions), a *named* Agent call launches a teammate, not a subagent: its
   returns come back as idle notifications, cut off at a fixed length and arriving late and twice,
   and the resume carries no `<usage>` block, so the dial below goes blind. Unnamed, it stays a
   subagent in every mode — its result arrives whole, once, with its token count — and it is still
   resumable by `SendMessage` to the held ID. (Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents § Subagent
   names; verified across 23 session transcripts 2026-09-26 — the failures were exactly the named
   spawns in CLI sessions.)
2. **Every later address → resume the same agent** (`SendMessage` to the held ID), naming the
   posture and filling that posture prompt's slots. It carries its prior context forward — don't
   re-spawn, and don't re-feed what it already holds. After a compaction the ID may be missing from the summary: find it in the session's `subagents/` folder and resume that one before spawning another ([[Concierge]] § The mechanism).
3. **Watch its health with the dial.** Each resume returns `subagent_tokens` in the Agent tool's
   `<usage>` block — the objective read (never its self-report). Pass it to the dial:
   `node _ops/concierge/dial.mjs --tokens <N> --model <companion-model>`. Headline is **trust** = capacity
   (÷ window): fine below ~60%, watch 60–80%, degraded past 80% — only capacity says respawn-for-reliability.
   A separate **cost** note (from absolute load) flags when resumes get expensive — respawn-to-save, not a
   trust alarm. Parked between addresses it costs nothing. Same dial serves the close (`--for close`), where
   how spent the parent is leads.

If you expect a genuinely large fan-out, tell Loudon the rough cost first (his standing preference).

## Triage — classify the address, name the posture

| The address sounds like… | Posture | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| "find / collect / gather every doc/link/entry about X" — wants the **material** | **gatherer** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/gatherer.md` |
| "what does the palace say about X / how does Z work" — wants an **answer** | **oracle Q&A** (read-only, may web-verify) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/oracle-qa.md` |
| "what should I work on / what's open / I'm back" — wants **one move**, not a pile | **scout** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/scout.md` |
| "tidy / tend the links around what I touched" | **curator** (writes) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/curator.md` |
| "close this session well" | **moderator** (at the close) | not this skill — the `close well` trigger, which **resumes this same resident** by the ID you held (`_ops/closing-well/dispatch.md` § Path A) |
| anything a cheap file-read settles | — | just read the file; don't address |

Fill the posture prompt's slots — `{{REQUEST}}` / `{{QUESTION}}` / `{{TOUCHED_ENTRIES}}`,
`{{TRANSCRIPT_CONTEXT}}`, `{{PALACE_ROOT}}` = the palace folder this session was started in: its
worktree or clone, and `/Users/loudonstearns/Documents/The Palace` only when the session runs there.
For a conversation-dependent address, distill the transcript
(`node _ops/closing-well/transcript-reader.mjs --resolve --session <id>` → `--distill --session <id>`); for a self-contained
one, a 2–3 line note is enough.

## Relay — and hold the safety line

Relay the product as returned (already file-cited). For the **curator**: report what it *did*
(reversible), **surface its `offer`s for Loudon's yes; on his yes, address the Concierge again to apply them — the child session does not write the house**, and pass
along its flags and anything it web-verified. The companion's heavy bias is to draft, not act;
your job on the other end is to keep the review real — drafts get read, not rubber-stamped.
Hand each offer on as the curator wrote it — its plain sentence, every rule it writes down, its exact words — and if you have promised Loudon the words, show them; a summary in their place is said aloud as a summary.

## The guard (carry it every time)

The companion is a **faster path to ground truth, never a replacement** ([[Concierge]] § The
guard). Every line it returns is a clickable file pointer to verify; git stays ground truth; the
palace's silence is a real answer, never a confabulated one. Keep this shim thin — when the model
changes, change `_ops/concierge/README.md`, `prompts/companion.md`, and the canon entry, not this

1	# rich-face — the renderer behind [[Enrichment]]
2	
3	An entry's **rich face**: the entry's own words as the spine, read live from its `.md`, with the
4	sound, image and interactive pieces [[Enrichment]] made or gathered laid beside the headings they
5	serve. The ceremony (when and how to enrich a page) is `Enrichment.md`; this folder is the machinery.
6	
7	## Open one
8	
9	- From an entry in STIGMERGY: the face switch (`F`), when the entry's bundle holds the manifest.
10	- With STIGMERGY running: `http://localhost:5173/rich/?entry=Kuramoto%20Coupling`
11	- Standalone: `node _ops/rich-face/rich-server.mjs [--root <palace>] [--detach]` prints its URL, on a
12	  port leased to it (8850–8949), so several sessions can preview several palaces at once; its pieces
13	  run on a second leased port, a piece origin of its own, as STIGMERGY's do; add
14	  `?entry=Kuramoto%20Coupling`. `--stop [port]` stops your own, `--list` shows them. Reviews reach
15	  STIGMERGY's board only when started with `--app http://localhost:5173`. The app README's
16	  § A preview of your own, on a leased port has the rest.
17	- Public: the read view ships this page static under `rich/`. `_ops/stigmergy/app/scripts/build-public.mjs`
18	  marks the page `<meta name="rich:static">`, so its lookups come from the snapshot (`data/rich.json`),
19	  its text is the snapshot's rather than re-read live, and nothing is posted.
20	
21	Any entry opens. `&review=0` hides the review layer.
22	
23	## Files
24	
25	| file | what it does |
26	|---|---|
27	| `parse.js` | entry → sections → prose blocks and figures; the section fingerprint. Shared by the page and `fingerprint.mjs`, so a stamp and a check can't disagree. |
28	| `rich.html` | the page: its markup and styles. Its one script is `rich.js`. All its URLs are relative, so it works at `/` and at `/rich/`. |
29	| `rich.js` | the renderer, served as `_rich/rich.js` so the page can carry `script-src 'self'`. It reads the `.md` every few seconds, lays prose, figures and manifest pieces, frames each piece from its plan, marks drift, and carries the review dock. |
30	| `rich-handler.mjs` | the request handler: renderer + palace files (byte ranges), `_api/resolve`, `_api/find`, `_api/media`, `_api/review` → STIGMERGY `POST /api/persistent` as a `human_eval`. Mounted by STIGMERGY (`app/server/api/rich.js`) and by `rich-server.mjs`. |
31	| `rich-server.mjs` | the standalone server, the preview: any palace root, on a port leased from `_ops/commons/port-lease.mjs` |
32	| `resolve.mjs` | the one resolver: the page, `fingerprint.mjs` and the public build find an entry, or the file a reference names, the same way, from git's index. A miss comes back with a one-line label the page shows in the figure's place. |
33	| `contract.mjs` | the piece contract in one place: a piece's own declaration, its manifest entry's `contract` block and `grants.json` become how the piece is framed, its chips and mark, and the Permissions-Policy and CSP it is sent with. The page, the deck, the piece origin and the public build all ask here. |
34	| `piece-origin.mjs` | the piece origin: the listener every piece runs on, `127.0.0.1:8843` beside STIGMERGY's 5173, and on a second leased port beside a standalone preview (below). |
35	| `conform.mjs` | the piece checker: every piece against its declaration and its code, its pins against the shelf, how a face names its files, and, in headless Chromium, its console, height, play and hush. Report-only; `conform.json` holds the two enforce switches (off), the pages that are never pieces, and reviewed exceptions. `"<Entry>"`, `--all`, or named pages. |
36	| `libs.json` | the library shelf: every library a piece may load from a CDN, at an exact version with its SRI hash, and the loose spellings each pin replaces |
37	| `pin-cdn.mjs` | the shelf's one writer: `--add <url>` puts a library on it; given pages, it pins their CDN tags to the shelf (url, `integrity`, `crossorigin`). It shows a diff and a digest first, and `--write <digest>` writes only that, only to files unchanged since |
38	| `untracked.mjs` | every file a face names that git doesn't track, with the step that tracks it (§ Media a face plays). The checker's `file-local` carries the same steps |
39	| `check-kuramoto-pieces.mjs` | re-checks the physics claims of Kuramoto's pieces headless, on their own worklet code |
40	| `kit/` | the piece kit (`piece.js`) and the one function every server injects it through (`inject.mjs`) |
41	| `serve-file.mjs` | sends one file: its type, byte ranges, and a web page as a piece with the kit injected. The handler and the piece origin both send files through it. |
42	| `grants.json` | what Loudon has let a piece use: camera, microphone, midi, hosts. One line per piece, written only on his yes. |
43	| `fingerprint.mjs` | section fingerprints and drift; `--stamp [section…]` records the "still true" verdict |
44	| `manifests/` | a workshop home for a manifest before its entry is placed; a manifest in the entry's bundle wins, and the face switch offers only the bundle's |
45	
46	## The manifest — `[Entry]/[Entry] — rich.json`
47	
48	Self-describing like any bundle file (`title`, `born`, `links`, `forward_vector`), then:
49	
50	```json
51	{ "entry": "…", "tier": "sketch|study|piece", "made": "YYYY-MM-DD", "round": 1,
52	  "page": { "bed": { "file": "…wav", "volume": 0.14 } },
53	  "sections": [ { "heading": "In Our Instruments", "made_against": "<12 hex>", "made": "…", "stamped": "…",
54	      "pieces": [ { "file": "…", "origin": "made|gathered", "by": "…", "title": "…", "caption": "…",
55	                    "near": "<a phrase in a paragraph | a figure's filename>", "place": "margin|band", "height": 640,
56	                    "contract": { "needs": "camera", "files": "frames.json", "size": "fill 4/3" } } ] } ] }
57	```
58	
59	A section is named by its heading. When the text repeats a heading, the repeat is named with its
60	place — the second `## Notes` is `"heading": "Notes (2)"` — and `fingerprint.mjs --stamp "Notes (2)"`
61	reaches it the same way.
62	
63	Every file the text or the manifest names is found by `resolve.mjs`, the same way live and in the read
64	view. `/…` is palace-absolute. A path with a slash is tried beside the `.md`, then from the palace root,
65	then in the entry's bundle, and never by its last name alone. A bare name is looked up in the bundle (its
66	top folder, then anywhere under it), then across the palace, and each step counts only if exactly one
67	file has that name. The index is git's. On the live page it holds tracked files, new files git doesn't
68	ignore, and the sound, video and images git ignores. In the public build it holds committed files only, so
69	a build on the Mac publishes what CI's would (§ Media a face plays). A hidden folder, any other file git
70	ignores, a symlink that leads outside the palace, or a name in the wrong case is refused. At each step,
71	where a bare name could mean a tracked file or one git doesn't track, the tracked one wins.
72	A file that doesn't resolve shows as a labelled box in the figure's place, naming the file and why, e.g.
73	`3 files are named “index.html” (…). Give its path to choose one.` `near` anchors
74	a piece right after that paragraph or figure; otherwise it goes at the section's end. Audio, images and
75	text pieces default to the margin; video, interactives and diagrams to the band. An interactive's
76	`height` (px) is its size until the piece reports its own. Every served piece reports through the kit
77	(below), so the manifest `height` matters for what the kit can't measure: a piece sized by the viewport,
78	or one with nothing laid out. With neither, 800. Kuramoto's were measured in a 1130 px column.
79	
80	`contract` is for a gathered proof nobody should edit: the manifest speaks for it, with the same fields a
81	piece declares in its own head (below). A piece that declares for itself is held to its own words.
82	
83	## Media a face plays: what git tracks is what the public face has
84	
85	The live page may play a file that is only on this Mac; the public build plays only what git tracks.
86	Loudon, 2026-10-20: "the rich face can play on a local machine if the files are only on the local
87	machine, if public, then they can't play, unfortunately. I would like, if possible, to decide to place
88	audio needed for rich faces in git, so they can be played." So the media a face needs is placed in git
89	on purpose, chosen with care, and not left ignored.
90	
91	- **On the live page.** The resolver finds a file git doesn't track: a new file not yet committed, or a
92	  sound, video or image git ignores, such as a steward's render under `Projects/` or `Shop/Shopkeeper/`.
93	  The file plays, and its figure carries the chip `only on this Mac` (for a piece's declared files,
94	  `files · N only on this Mac`). The page's head lists every such file the face names, pieces' declared
95	  files included. Nothing else git ignores is ever served.
96	- **In the public build.** The build ships only committed files. A file it can't ship but this Mac has
97	  shows as a labelled box: `“take-07.wav” is only on this Mac: track it to publish.` A build in CI, which
98	  has no such file, shows the plain miss. A tracked file over 25 MB is left out too, and its box says so,
99	  so keep a take a face needs under that.
100	- **To publish one.** `node _ops/rich-face/untracked.mjs ["<Entry>"]` lists every file a face names that
101	  git doesn't track, with the step for each. It exits 1 while any is left. The checker reports each such
102	  file as `file-local`, a warning, with the same step; in a build, a file this Mac has but git doesn't
103	  track is reported as `file-local`, not as a miss.
104	  - A new file: commit it through the palace committer.
105	  - A steward's render: copy it into its entry's bundle under `rich-face/`, which `.gitignore` keeps
106	    (`!Projects/**/rich-face/**`, `!Shop/Shopkeeper/**/rich-face/**`), and commit the copy.
107	
108	  Once the copy is committed, the face names it as before. A bare name lands on the tracked copy, even
109	  when the render sits in the bundle's own top folder.
110	  The steward's render stays ignored where it is. A new render of the same take changes nothing until
111	  someone copies it again on purpose.
112	- **Not `git add -f`.** The committer stages a path with a plain `git add`, which refuses an ignored
113	  file. And once an ignored file is force-tracked, every re-render of it that the steward posts would
114	  ride into its next cycle commit.
115	- **Choose with care.** A take copied into `rich-face/` stays in git's history for good. So the public
116	  face grows by what a face is worth playing, not by every render.
117	
118	## The parser's rules
119	
120	- `# Title` opens the first section; each `##` opens the next. Deeper headings stay inside.
121	  Blank lines before the first heading open nothing; anything else there joins the H1's section
122	  (with no H1, it opens a section keyed to the title). No two sections ever share a key: a heading
123	  the text repeats (case and emphasis don't count) gets its place after it — `Notes (2)` — while every
124	  heading's first use, including one written `Notes (2)`, keeps its own.
125	- What a file is — video, audio, image, interactive — comes from one list in `parse.js` (`mediaKind`,
126	  `isMedia`); `rich.html` keeps none of its own.
127	- A figure is a blockquote holding media (its prose is the caption; a line that is only media —
128	  `![[file]]`, `[[file.ext|label]]` or `[label](file.ext)` — is not), a paragraph that is only an embed
129	  (an italic line right after it is the caption), or a ```` ```mermaid ```` fence.
130	- A legacy **door** — any line linking `/rich/?entry=` — is still dropped, as tolerance: the rich face
131	  never shows that line (the words around it stay; it is never a caption) and it never counts toward a
132	  fingerprint. Inside a code fence it is only text. A reader reaches the rich face by the face switch
133	  now, which offers it when the entry's bundle holds the manifest — not by a line in the body.
134	- A section's fingerprint is SHA-256 (first 12 hex) of its prose blocks, whitespace-collapsed. Figures'
135	  captions don't count — they travel with their media.
136	
137	## What the page lets run
138	
139	The page is served from STIGMERGY's origin, so anything that runs in it runs as STIGMERGY. So nothing the
140	palace writes runs there: every piece runs on the **piece origin**.
141	
142	- **The piece origin.** STIGMERGY starts a second listener, `piece-origin.mjs`, on `127.0.0.1:8843`; a
143	  standalone preview (`rich-server.mjs`) starts its own on a second leased port.
144	  `STIGMERGY_PIECE_PORT` names another port, and any STIGMERGY not on 5173 takes a free one. `127.0.0.1` is
145	  another site from `localhost`, so whatever a piece sends toward STIGMERGY is cross-site: the request
146	  guard refuses its writes and `/api/open`, and STIGMERGY sends no CORS, so a piece can't read what comes
147	  back. The piece origin answers GET and HEAD for its exact Host, with no CORS. It serves only registered
148	  pieces, the files they declare, and the design-system folder (not its review layer, whose notes land in
149	  storage a face does not keep). A piece is registered from every face (each manifest's pieces and its
150	  entry's text figures) at boot and again on a miss, and whenever the page or the deck asks to frame it.
151	  Anything else gets a 404 that says why. Every file goes out with nosniff. The design system's files go
152	  out with CORP cross-origin, since a piece with no origin of its own loads them too; a piece and its
153	  declared files, same-origin. If the port is taken, every piece's figure says so. A piece never falls
154	  back to the page's origin.
155	- **Each frame is built from the piece's plan** (`contract.mjs`). A piece that declares nothing is
156	  **pre-contract**. It runs `sandbox="allow-scripts"` in an opaque origin, as every piece ran before, and so
157	  does a declared piece that needs nothing of an origin (only `net`, `fill` or fullscreen). A piece that
158	  needs a device, storage or a declared file also gets `allow-same-origin`, and only after the page has
159	  checked that the piece's URL is on another origin than its own. A camera, microphone or midi reaches a
160	  piece only when both its frame's `allow` and the piece origin's `Permissions-Policy` say so, and both
161	  come from `grants.json`, so a frame that asks for more gets nothing. Each piece is also sent with a CSP:
162	  scripts from the piece origin, inline, and the shelf's CDNs (every origin `libs.json` names); fetches only to the
163	  piece origin and its granted hosts. The CSP is report-only for its first round.
164	- **The figure says what its piece uses.** Each figure carries a mark (introduced, pre-contract or
165	  errored) and a chip for each need, declared file count, host and `fill`. A missing grant line shows as
166	  `camera · not granted`. A cap that bites is named under the frame: a height outside 120 to 8000 px, a
167	  piece sized by its own window, or a piece that never reported a height. A piece whose script fails is
168	  marked errored, and its first error shows under the frame.
169	- **The page's own script is its own file.** `rich.html` loads `_rich/rich.js` and carries
170	  `Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none';
171	  frame-src <the piece origin>`. So an entry's text that slipped past the sanitizer still runs nothing.
172	  Mermaid renders under it (proven in headless Chromium).
173	- **The server sandboxes a piece reached any other way.** Every palace `.html`, `.htm` and `.svg` under
174	  `/rich/<path>` (and STIGMERGY's `GET /api/file`) is sent with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox
175	  allow-scripts`. A piece opened from a link in the prose or in a new tab still runs in an opaque origin.

# rich-face — the renderer behind [[Enrichment]]

An entry's **rich face**: the entry's own words as the spine, read live from its `.md`, with the
sound, image and interactive pieces [[Enrichment]] made or gathered laid beside the headings they
serve. The ceremony (when and how to enrich a page) is `Enrichment.md`; this folder is the machinery.

## Open one

- From an entry in STIGMERGY: the face switch (`F`), when the entry's bundle holds the manifest.
- With STIGMERGY running: `http://localhost:5173/rich/?entry=Kuramoto%20Coupling`
- Standalone: `node _ops/rich-face/rich-server.mjs [--root <palace>] [--detach]` prints its URL, on a
  port leased to it (8850–8949), so several sessions can preview several palaces at once; its pieces
  run on a second leased port, a piece origin of its own, as STIGMERGY's do; add
  `?entry=Kuramoto%20Coupling`. `--stop [port]` stops your own, `--list` shows them. Reviews reach
  STIGMERGY's board only when started with `--app http://localhost:5173`. The app README's
  § A preview of your own, on a leased port has the rest.
- Public: the read view ships this page static under `rich/`. `_ops/stigmergy/app/scripts/build-public.mjs`
  marks the page `<meta name="rich:static">`, so its lookups come from the snapshot (`data/rich.json`),
  its text is the snapshot's rather than re-read live, and nothing is posted.

Any entry opens. `&review=0` hides the review layer.

## Files

| file | what it does |
|---|---|
| `parse.js` | entry → sections → prose blocks and figures; the section fingerprint. Shared by the page and `fingerprint.mjs`, so a stamp and a check can't disagree. |
| `rich.html` | the page: its markup and styles. Its one script is `rich.js`. All its URLs are relative, so it works at `/` and at `/rich/`. |
| `rich.js` | the renderer, served as `_rich/rich.js` so the page can carry `script-src 'self'`. It reads the `.md` every few seconds, lays prose, figures and manifest pieces, frames each piece from its plan, marks drift, and carries the review dock. |
| `rich-handler.mjs` | the request handler: renderer + palace files (byte ranges), `_api/resolve`, `_api/find`, `_api/media`, `_api/review` → STIGMERGY `POST /api/persistent` as a `human_eval`. Mounted by STIGMERGY (`app/server/api/rich.js`) and by `rich-server.mjs`. |
| `rich-server.mjs` | the standalone server, the preview: any palace root, on a port leased from `_ops/commons/port-lease.mjs` |
| `resolve.mjs` | the one resolver: the page, `fingerprint.mjs` and the public build find an entry, or the file a reference names, the same way, from git's index. A miss comes back with a one-line label the page shows in the figure's place. |
| `contract.mjs` | the piece contract in one place: a piece's own declaration, its manifest entry's `contract` block and `grants.json` become how the piece is framed, its chips and mark, and the Permissions-Policy and CSP it is sent with. The page, the deck, the piece origin and the public build all ask here. |
| `piece-origin.mjs` | the piece origin: the listener every piece runs on, `127.0.0.1:8843` beside STIGMERGY's 5173, and on a second leased port beside a standalone preview (below). |
| `conform.mjs` | the piece checker: every piece against its declaration and its code, its pins against the shelf, how a face names its files, and, in headless Chromium, its console, height, play and hush. Report-only; `conform.json` holds the two enforce switches (off), the pages that are never pieces, and reviewed exceptions. `"<Entry>"`, `--all`, or named pages. |
| `libs.json` | the library shelf: every library a piece may load from a CDN, at an exact version with its SRI hash, and the loose spellings each pin replaces |
| `pin-cdn.mjs` | the shelf's one writer: `--add <url>` puts a library on it; given pages, it pins their CDN tags to the shelf (url, `integrity`, `crossorigin`). It shows a diff and a digest first, and `--write <digest>` writes only that, only to files unchanged since |
| `untracked.mjs` | every file a face names that git doesn't track, with the step that tracks it (§ Media a face plays). The checker's `file-local` carries the same steps |
| `check-kuramoto-pieces.mjs` | re-checks the physics claims of Kuramoto's pieces headless, on their own worklet code |
| `kit/` | the piece kit (`piece.js`) and the one function every server injects it through (`inject.mjs`) |
| `serve-file.mjs` | sends one file: its type, byte ranges, and a web page as a piece with the kit injected. The handler and the piece origin both send files through it. |

Self-describing like any bundle file (`title`, `born`, `links`, `forward_vector`), then:

The live page may play a file that is only on this Mac; the public build plays only what git tracks.
